items.q: A consumer is in equilibrium over two commodities. The marginal utility of the last unit of maize bought is 240 and maize costs N20 per unit. If beans cost N10 per unit, what marginal utility of beans is needed for equilibrium?
items.s: Equilibrium needs marginal utility of maize divided by its price to equal marginal utility of beans divided by its price, so marginal utility of beans = 240 x 10 / 20 = 120.

items.q: A consumer's total utility from a commodity is 350 after two units and 390 after three units. Find the marginal utility of the third unit.
items.s: Marginal utility of the third unit = total utility after three units less total utility after two units = 390 - 350 = 40.

items.q: The price of palm oil rises by 5 per cent and the quantity demanded falls by 25 per cent. Calculate the price elasticity of demand.
items.s: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity divided by percentage change in price = 25 / 5 = 5.

items.q: A rise of 12 per cent in the price of yam raises the quantity supplied by 12 per cent. Find the elasticity of supply.
items.s: Elasticity of supply = percentage change in quantity supplied / percentage change in price = 12 / 12 = 1.

items.q: When the labour force rises from 3 to 7 workers the total output of a farm rises from 300 kg to 400 kg. Find the marginal product of the extra workers in kg per worker.
items.s: Marginal product = change in output / change in labour = (400 - 300) / (7 - 3) = 25 kg per worker.

items.q: The total product of a variable input L on a farm is TP = 25L + 24L^2 - 3L^3. Find the marginal product when L is 2 units.
items.s: Marginal product is the slope of total product, 25 + 48L - 9L^2, which at L = 2 gives 25 + 96 - 36 = 85.

items.q: At the least cost combination on a farm the marginal product of labour is 40 kg and the wage rate is N500 per worker, while the marginal product of capital is 12 kg. Find the price of capital per unit.
items.s: Least cost requires marginal product of labour / wage = marginal product of capital / price of capital, so price of capital = 12 x 500 / 40 = 150.

items.q: A production possibility curve shows that a farm can produce 400 kg of maize with 250 kg of cowpea, or 550 kg of maize with 500 kg of cowpea. Find the marginal rate of product transformation of maize for cowpea.
items.s: Rate of transformation = maize given up / cowpea gained = (400 - 550) / (500 - 250) = -0.6 kg of maize per kg of cowpea.

items.q: A poultry farm's total cost of production for the season is N380000 and its total variable cost is N320000. Find the total fixed cost.
items.s: Total fixed cost = total cost less total variable cost = N380000 - N320000 = N60000.

items.q: A farm producing 400 kg of output carries fixed costs of N40000. Find the average fixed cost per kg.
items.s: Average fixed cost = fixed cost / output = N40000 / 400 kg = N100 per kg.

items.q: A farm sells 200 kg of produce at N600 per kg. Its fixed costs are N50000 and its variable cost is N150 per kg. Find the profit.
When a farmer increases every input by 10 per cent, total output rises by 75 per cent. Find the elasticity of scale.
items.s: Elasticity of scale = percentage change in output / percentage change in all inputs = 75 / 10 = 7.5.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: A farm producing 100 tonnes at a total cost of N8000 expands to 200 tonnes at a total cost of N14400. Find the average cost per tonne at the larger size.
items.s: Average cost = total cost / output = N14400 / 200 tonnes = N72 per tonne.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 80 - 4Q and has a constant marginal cost of N40 per unit. Find the output that maximises profit.
items.s: Marginal revenue is 80 - 8Q. Setting it equal to marginal cost: 80 - 8Q = 40, so Q = 40 / 8 = 5 units.

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 100 - 2Q. Find the output at which total revenue is greatest.
items.s: Total revenue = 100Q - 2Q^2, which peaks where 100 - 4Q = 0, that is at Q = 25 units.

items.q: In the market for sorghum the quantity demanded is Qd = 220 - 10P and the quantity supplied is Qs = 100 + 20P. Find the equilibrium price.
items.s: At equilibrium 220 - 10P = 100 + 20P, so 30P = 120 and P = 4.

items.q: The demand for garri in a town is Qd = 400 - 50P. Find the quantity demanded at a price of N4 per kg.
items.s: Substituting P = 4 gives Qd = 400 - 50 x 4 = 200 kg.

items.q: One more bag of fertilizer applied to a maize plot raises output by 15 kg, and maize sells at N300 per kg. Find the marginal value product of a bag.
items.s: Marginal value product = extra output x price = 15 kg x N300 = N4500.

items.q: The marginal value product of a bag of fertilizer is N8000 and a bag costs N4000. Find the value of extra output obtained per naira spent on fertilizer.
items.s: Value of extra output per naira = N8000 / N4000 = N2.

items.q: At the present level of fertilizer use on a farm the marginal product of the input is 15 kg and the average product is 100 kg. Find the elasticity of production.
items.s: Elasticity of production = marginal product / average product = 15 / 100 = 0.15.

items.q: A farm's total receipts for the season are N800000 and fertilizer accounts for 10 per cent of them. Find the amount paid out to the fertilizer supplier.
items.s: Amount paid = 10 per cent of N800000 = N80000.

items.q: A consumer pays N420 per kg for rice while the farmer receives N300 per kg at the farm gate. Find the marketing margin per kg.
items.s: Marketing margin = price paid by the final buyer less price received by the producer = N420 - N300 = N120 per kg.

items.q: Government pays a subsidy of N800 per bag on 5000 bags of fertilizer distributed to farmers. Find the total subsidy paid.
items.s: Total subsidy = subsidy per bag x number of bags = N800 x 5000 = N4000000.

items.q: At the guaranteed price of N600 per kg, consumers demand 300 tonnes of grain while farmers supply 450 tonnes. Find the surplus that government must buy.
items.s: Surplus bought = quantity supplied - quantity demanded = 450 - 300 = 150 tonnes.

items.q: At a controlled price of N300 per kg, farmers supply 200 tonnes of grain while consumers demand 300 tonnes. Find the shortage in the market.
items.s: Shortage = quantity demanded - quantity supplied = 300 - 200 = 100 tonnes.

items.q: A buyer is willing to pay up to N2000 per kg for rice but actually pays N900 per kg for 40 kg. Find the consumer surplus.
items.s: Consumer surplus = (willingness to pay - price paid) x quantity = (N2000 - N900) x 40 = N44000.

items.q: When the price of butter rises by 5 per cent the quantity of margarine bought rises by 6 per cent. Find the cross elasticity of demand for margarine.
items.s: Cross elasticity = percentage change in quantity of margarine / percentage change in price of butter = 6 / 5 = 1.2.

items.q: Demand for eggs falls from 200 to 170 crates when the price rises from N80 to N88 per crate. Using the arc formula, find the price elasticity of demand.
A farm's total product curve for a variable input L is TP = 20L + 24L^2 - 3L^3. Find the level of L at which the average product of the input is at its maximum.
items.s: Average product = 20 + 24L - 3L^2, whose slope is 24 - 6L; setting that slope to nil gives L = 24 / 6 = 4 units.

items.q: An isoquant shows that 500 kg of maize can be produced with 60 units of capital and 5 units of labour, or with 45 units of capital and 10 units of labour. Find the marginal rate of technical substitution of labour for capital.
items.s: Marginal rate of technical substitution = capital given up / labour added = (60 - 45) / (10 - 5) = 3 units of capital per unit of labour.

items.q: A farm has fixed costs of N100000 and variable costs of N120000 while producing 200 kg of output. Find the average total cost per kg.
items.s: Average total cost = (fixed cost + variable cost) / output = (N100000 + N120000) / 200 kg = N1100 per kg.

items.q: A farm's total cost is N100000 when output is 20 units and N105000 when output is 45 units. Find the marginal cost of the extra units.
items.s: Marginal cost = change in total cost / change in output = (N105000 - N100000) / (45 - 20) = N200 per unit.

items.q: A maize farmer sells in a perfectly competitive market at N800 per kg. Marginal cost is MC = 600 + 25Q in naira per kg. Find the output at which profit is greatest.
items.s: In perfect competition profit is greatest where price equals marginal cost: 800 = 600 + 25Q, so Q = 200 / 25 = 8 kg.

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 120 - 5Q. Find its marginal revenue at an output of 4 units.
items.s: Total revenue = 120Q - 5Q^2, so marginal revenue = 120 - 10Q, which at Q = 4 gives 80.

items.q: The demand for garri is Qd = 180 - 10P and the supply is Qs = 60 + 10P. Find the equilibrium quantity.
items.s: Setting 180 - 10P = 60 + 10P gives P = 6. Quantity = 60 + 10 x 6 = 120 units.

items.q: Rice sells to consumers at N500 per kg and the farmer receives N180 per kg. Find the producer's share of the consumer price as a percentage.
items.s: Producer's share = (N180 / N500) x 100 = 36 per cent.

items.q: A farmer would have accepted N800 per kg for maize but actually received N1200 per kg on 50 kg. Find the producer surplus.
items.s: Producer surplus = (price received - least acceptable price) x quantity = (N1200 - N800) x 50 = N20000.

items.q: The marginal utilities of the first, second and third units of a farm product consumed by a household are 90, 25 and 10. Find the total utility of three units.
items.s: Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities = 90 + 25 + 10 = 125.

items.q: A consumer is in equilibrium over two commodities. The marginal utility of the last unit of maize bought is 300 and maize costs N50 per unit. If beans cost N20 per unit, what marginal utility of beans is needed for equilibrium?
items.s: Equilibrium needs marginal utility of maize divided by its price to equal marginal utility of beans divided by its price, so marginal utility of beans = 300 x 20 / 50 = 120.

items.q: A consumer's total utility from a commodity is 260 after two units and 290 after three units. Find the marginal utility of the third unit.
items.s: Marginal utility of the third unit = total utility after three units less total utility after two units = 290 - 260 = 30.

items.q: The price of palm oil rises by 20 per cent and the quantity demanded falls by 30 per cent. Calculate the price elasticity of demand.
items.s: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity divided by percentage change in price = 30 / 20 = 1.5.

items.q: A rise of 8 per cent in the price of yam raises the quantity supplied by 18 per cent. Find the elasticity of supply.
items.s: Elasticity of supply = percentage change in quantity supplied / percentage change in price = 18 / 8 = 2.25.

items.q: A farm employing 12 workers produces 480 kg of grain in a season. Find the average product of labour in kg per worker.
items.s: Average product = total output / number of workers = 480 / 12 = 40 kg per worker.

items.q: When the labour force rises from 5 to 8 workers the total output of a farm rises from 300 kg to 420 kg. Find the marginal product of the extra workers in kg per worker.
items.s: Marginal product = change in output / change in labour = (420 - 300) / (8 - 5) = 40 kg per worker.

items.q: The total product of a variable input L on a farm is TP = 10L + 30L^2 - 3L^3. Find the marginal product when L is 3 units.
items.s: Marginal product is the slope of total product, 10 + 60L - 9L^2, which at L = 3 gives 10 + 180 - 81 = 109.

items.q: At the least cost combination on a farm the marginal product of labour is 50 kg and the wage rate is N300 per worker, while the marginal product of capital is 25 kg. Find the price of capital per unit.
items.s: Least cost requires marginal product of labour / wage = marginal product of capital / price of capital, so price of capital = 25 x 300 / 50 = 150.

items.q: A production possibility curve shows that a farm can produce 500 kg of maize with 250 kg of cowpea, or 300 kg of maize with 500 kg of cowpea. Find the marginal rate of product transformation of maize for cowpea.
items.s: Rate of transformation = maize given up / cowpea gained = (500 - 300) / (500 - 250) = 0.8 kg of maize per kg of cowpea.

items.q: A poultry farm's total cost of production for the season is N330000 and its total variable cost is N180000. Find the total fixed cost.
items.s: Total fixed cost = total cost less total variable cost = N330000 - N180000 = N150000.

items.q: A farm produces 200 kg of grain at a total variable cost of N10000. Find the average variable cost per kg.
items.s: Average variable cost = total variable cost / output = N10000 / 200 kg = N50 per kg.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs”
o: Least cost combination
Complementary enterprises
Expansion path
Production possibility curve
items.s: Expansion path is the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs.

items.q: Average product may be defined as
o: the range from the maximum of average output to the point where extra output becomes nil
a factor whose quantity cannot be altered within the production period
the output obtained per unit of the variable input employed
a factor whose quantity can be altered within the production period
items.s: Average product: the output obtained per unit of the variable input employed. The other options describe Rational stage, Variable input, Fixed input.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Elastic demand?
o: the responsiveness of the quantity offered for sale to a change in the amount charged
the ratio of the percentage change in quantity bought to the percentage change in the buyer's earnings
the responsiveness of the quantity of one commodity bought to a change in the amount charged for another
a case in which the quantity bought changes by a larger percentage than the amount charged
items.s: Elastic demand: a case in which the quantity bought changes by a larger percentage than the amount charged. The other options describe Elasticity of supply, Income elasticity of demand, Cross elasticity of demand.

items.q: Marginal rate of technical substitution is best described as
o: the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs
the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant
farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other
the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount
items.s: Marginal rate of technical substitution: the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant. The other options describe Expansion path, Complementary enterprises, Isocost line.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Indifference curve.
o: the satisfaction a person obtains from consuming a commodity
a line joining combinations of two commodities that give a consumer equal satisfaction
the change in the quantity bought when a commodity becomes relatively cheaper with satisfaction held constant
the change in the quantity bought that follows from a change in real purchasing power
items.s: Indifference curve: a line joining combinations of two commodities that give a consumer equal satisfaction. The other options describe Substitution effect, Income effect, Utility.

items.q: Public good is best described as
o: a situation in which nobody can be made better off without making someone else worse off
a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive
the use of resources in the mix of commodities that people value most
the fall in total well-being when the quantity traded differs from the best quantity
items.s: Public good: a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive. The other options describe Pareto efficiency, Deadweight loss, Allocative efficiency.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Average total cost?
o: the variable expense per unit of output
the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced
the sum of all expenses incurred in producing a given level of output
the addition to total expense from producing one more unit of output
items.s: Average total cost: the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced. The other options describe Average variable cost, Marginal cost, Total cost.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Marginal revenue?
o: the ratio of extra output to average output at a given level of input use
the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input
the addition to total receipts from selling one more unit of output
the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input
items.s: Marginal revenue: the addition to total receipts from selling one more unit of output. The other options describe Elasticity of production, Marginal factor cost, Marginal value product.

items.q: Law of diminishing marginal utility may be defined as
o: a line joining combinations of two commodities that give a consumer equal satisfaction
the change in the quantity bought that follows from a change in real purchasing power
the principle that each extra unit consumed adds less satisfaction than the unit before it
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of a commodity consumed
items.s: Law of diminishing marginal utility: the principle that each extra unit consumed adds less satisfaction than the unit before it. The other options describe Income effect, Total utility, Indifference curve.

items.q: Which term is described by “the combinations of two commodities that a consumer can buy with a given income at given prices”?
o: Income effect
Substitution effect
Marginal utility
Budget line
items.s: Budget line is the combinations of two commodities that a consumer can buy with a given income at given prices.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Variable input?
o: the technical relationship between the quantities of inputs used and the output obtained
a curve showing all combinations of two inputs that yield the same output
the principle that beyond some point each extra unit of a variable input adds less to output than the unit before
a factor whose quantity can be altered within the production period
items.s: Variable input: a factor whose quantity can be altered within the production period. The other options describe Production function, Isoquant, Law of diminishing returns.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Isocost line?
o: the input mix at which the extra output per naira is equal for every input employed
farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other
a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources
the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount
items.s: Isocost line: the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount. The other options describe Least cost combination, Production possibility curve, Complementary enterprises.

items.q: Minimum efficient scale may be defined as
o: a situation in which output rises by a larger percentage than all inputs taken together
a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together
the reduction in average expense per unit as the size of the business grows
the smallest size at which average expense per unit reaches its lowest value
items.s: Minimum efficient scale: the smallest size at which average expense per unit reaches its lowest value. The other options describe Economies of scale, Increasing returns to scale, Decreasing returns to scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Which term is described by “the change in the quantity bought that follows from a change in real purchasing power”?
o: Consumer equilibrium
Income effect
Utility
Total utility
items.s: Income effect is the change in the quantity bought that follows from a change in real purchasing power.

items.q: Which term is described by “the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make”?
o: Derived demand
Elasticity of production
Marginal value product
Marginal revenue
items.s: Derived demand is the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make.

items.q: Price taker is best described as
o: a market of many small sellers of an identical commodity, none able to influence the ruling figure
a market dominated by a few large sellers whose decisions affect one another
conditions that make it difficult for new firms to join an industry
a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted
items.s: Price taker: a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted. The other options describe Barriers to entry, Oligopoly, Perfect competition.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Pareto efficiency?
o: a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction
a situation in which nobody can be made better off without making someone else worse off
the use of resources in the mix of commodities that people value most
a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive
items.s: Pareto efficiency: a situation in which nobody can be made better off without making someone else worse off. The other options describe Externality, Public good, Allocative efficiency.

items.q: Which term is described by “a situation in which output rises by a larger percentage than all inputs taken together”?
o: Returns to scale
Increasing returns to scale
Economies of scale
Constant returns to scale
items.s: Increasing returns to scale is a situation in which output rises by a larger percentage than all inputs taken together.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Variable input.
o: a curve showing all combinations of two inputs that yield the same output
a factor whose quantity can be altered within the production period
the whole output obtained from a given quantity of a variable input
the range from the maximum of average output to the point where extra output becomes nil
items.s: Variable input: a factor whose quantity can be altered within the production period. The other options describe Rational stage, Total product, Isoquant.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Price taker?
o: a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities
a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted
conditions that make it difficult for new firms to join an industry
a market dominated by a few large sellers whose decisions affect one another
items.s: Price taker: a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted. The other options describe Oligopoly, Barriers to entry, Monopolistic competition.

items.q: Constant returns to scale may be defined as
o: a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together
the reduction in average expense per unit as the size of the business grows
a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together
the response of output to a proportional change in all inputs together
items.s: Constant returns to scale: a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together. The other options describe Decreasing returns to scale, Returns to scale, Economies of scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Fixed cost may be defined as
o: an expense that does not vary with the level of output in the short run
the variable expense per unit of output
the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced
money already spent that no future decision can recover
items.s: Fixed cost: an expense that does not vary with the level of output in the short run. The other options describe Average total cost, Average variable cost, Sunk cost.

items.q: Monopolistic competition may be defined as
o: a market with exactly two sellers
a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities
the real or imagined differences that make buyers prefer one brand to another
a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted
items.s: Monopolistic competition: a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities. The other options describe Price taker, Product differentiation, Duopoly.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Monopolistic competition?
o: a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities
a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted
the practice of charging different buyers different amounts for the same commodity
a market of many small sellers of an identical commodity, none able to influence the ruling figure
items.s: Monopolistic competition: a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities. The other options describe Perfect competition, Price discrimination, Price taker.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive”
o: Public good
Externality
Pareto efficiency
Market failure
items.s: Public good is a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive.

items.q: Which term is described by “a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive”?
o: Public good
Deadweight loss
Allocative efficiency
Consumer surplus
items.s: Public good is a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive.

items.q: Total product may be defined as
o: the whole output obtained from a given quantity of a variable input
the extra output obtained by employing one more unit of a variable input
the output obtained per unit of the variable input employed
the principle that beyond some point each extra unit of a variable input adds less to output than the unit before
items.s: Total product: the whole output obtained from a given quantity of a variable input. The other options describe Law of diminishing returns, Average product, Marginal product.

items.q: Subsidy is best described as
o: a payment by government that lowers the expense of an input or commodity to the user
a store of grain held by government to steady supplies and prices
a legal maximum above which a commodity may not be sold
a legal minimum below which a commodity may not be sold
items.s: Subsidy: a payment by government that lowers the expense of an input or commodity to the user. The other options describe Price floor, Price ceiling, Buffer stock.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant”
o: Complementary enterprises
Marginal rate of product transformation
Least cost combination
Marginal rate of technical substitution
items.s: Marginal rate of technical substitution is the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant.

items.q: Marginal value product is best described as
o: the ratio of extra output to average output at a given level of input use
the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input
the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input
the payment for the use of land and other gifts of nature
items.s: Marginal value product: the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input. The other options describe Marginal factor cost, Economic rent, Elasticity of production.

items.q: Marginal factor cost may be defined as
o: the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make
the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input
the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input
the addition to total receipts from selling one more unit of output
items.s: Marginal factor cost: the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input. The other options describe Marginal revenue, Marginal value product, Derived demand.

items.q: Unitary elasticity is best described as
o: the responsiveness of the quantity of one commodity bought to a change in the amount charged for another
the case in which quantity bought and amount charged change by the same percentage
the responsiveness of the quantity bought to a change in the amount charged per unit
the ratio of the percentage change in quantity bought to the percentage change in the buyer's earnings
items.s: Unitary elasticity: the case in which quantity bought and amount charged change by the same percentage. The other options describe Income elasticity of demand, Price elasticity of demand, Cross elasticity of demand.

items.q: Which term is described by “farm activities that add income without reducing the output of the existing one”?
o: Complementary enterprises
Marginal rate of technical substitution
Supplementary enterprises
Expansion path
items.s: Supplementary enterprises is farm activities that add income without reducing the output of the existing one.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Monopolistic competition.
o: conditions that make it difficult for new firms to join an industry
a market with a single seller of a commodity that has no close substitute
a market with exactly two sellers
a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities
items.s: Monopolistic competition: a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities. The other options describe Barriers to entry, Monopoly, Duopoly.

items.q: Which term is described by “a factor whose quantity cannot be altered within the production period”?
o: Variable input
Marginal product
Production function
Fixed input
items.s: Fixed input is a factor whose quantity cannot be altered within the production period.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Arc elasticity?
o: responsiveness measured between two points using the average of those points as the base
the ratio of the percentage change in quantity bought to the percentage change in the buyer's earnings
the responsiveness of the quantity of one commodity bought to a change in the amount charged for another
the responsiveness of the quantity offered for sale to a change in the amount charged
items.s: Arc elasticity: responsiveness measured between two points using the average of those points as the base. The other options describe Cross elasticity of demand, Income elasticity of demand, Elasticity of supply.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “a legal minimum below which a commodity may not be sold”
o: Price ceiling
Support price
Price floor
Parity price
items.s: Price floor is a legal minimum below which a commodity may not be sold.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Supplementary enterprises?
o: the rate at which the output of one enterprise must fall for another to rise by one unit
the input mix at which the extra output per naira is equal for every input employed
farm activities that add income without reducing the output of the existing one
the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount
items.s: Supplementary enterprises: farm activities that add income without reducing the output of the existing one. The other options describe Isocost line, Marginal rate of product transformation, Least cost combination.

items.q: Total utility is best described as
o: the addition to satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a commodity
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of a commodity consumed
the change in the quantity bought that follows from a change in real purchasing power
the principle that each extra unit consumed adds less satisfaction than the unit before it
items.s: Total utility: the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of a commodity consumed. The other options describe Marginal utility, Law of diminishing marginal utility, Income effect.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the combination of commodities at which the consumer gets the greatest satisfaction from the money available”
o: Indifference curve
Marginal utility
Consumer equilibrium
Budget line
items.s: Consumer equilibrium is the combination of commodities at which the consumer gets the greatest satisfaction from the money available.

items.q: Production possibility curve may be defined as
o: farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other
a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources
the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant
the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount
items.s: Production possibility curve: a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources. The other options describe Isocost line, Marginal rate of technical substitution, Complementary enterprises.

items.q: Derived demand is best described as
o: the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input
the ratio of extra output to average output at a given level of input use
the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input
the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make
items.s: Derived demand: the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make. The other options describe Marginal factor cost, Elasticity of production, Factor share.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Support price?
o: a guaranteed minimum figure at which government stands ready to buy a commodity
a store of grain held by government to steady supplies and prices
a legal maximum above which a commodity may not be sold
the figure that gives a farm commodity the same buying power as in an earlier base period
items.s: Support price: a guaranteed minimum figure at which government stands ready to buy a commodity. The other options describe Buffer stock, Parity price, Price ceiling.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Marginal utility.
o: the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of a commodity consumed
the addition to satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a commodity
the principle that each extra unit consumed adds less satisfaction than the unit before it
the combination of commodities at which the consumer gets the greatest satisfaction from the money available
items.s: Marginal utility: the addition to satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a commodity. The other options describe Total utility, Law of diminishing marginal utility, Consumer equilibrium.

items.q: Factor share is best described as
o: the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make
the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input
the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input
the ratio of extra output to average output at a given level of input use
items.s: Factor share: the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input. The other options describe Elasticity of production, Marginal value product, Derived demand.

items.q: Which term is described by “the fixed expense divided by the number of units produced”?
o: Implicit cost
Average fixed cost
Variable cost
Marginal cost
items.s: Average fixed cost is the fixed expense divided by the number of units produced.

items.q: Which term is described by “a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together”?
o: Decreasing returns to scale
Increasing returns to scale
Diseconomies of scale
Returns to scale
items.s: Decreasing returns to scale is a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the variable expense per unit of output”
o: Average total cost
Average fixed cost
Fixed cost
Average variable cost
items.s: Average variable cost is the variable expense per unit of output.

items.q: Which term is described by “a market with exactly two sellers”?
o: Monopoly
Price discrimination
Duopoly
Perfect competition
items.s: Duopoly is a market with exactly two sellers.

items.q: Pareto efficiency is best described as
o: a situation in which nobody can be made better off without making someone else worse off
the use of resources in the mix of commodities that people value most
the difference between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid
a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction
items.s: Pareto efficiency: a situation in which nobody can be made better off without making someone else worse off. The other options describe Externality, Consumer surplus, Allocative efficiency.

items.q: Isocost line is best described as
o: the rate at which the output of one enterprise must fall for another to rise by one unit
the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount
the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs
a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources
items.s: Isocost line: the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount. The other options describe Production possibility curve, Expansion path, Marginal rate of product transformation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Least cost combination?
o: the input mix at which the extra output per naira is equal for every input employed
the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant
the rate at which the output of one enterprise must fall for another to rise by one unit
the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs
items.s: Least cost combination: the input mix at which the extra output per naira is equal for every input employed. The other options describe Marginal rate of product transformation, Expansion path, Marginal rate of technical substitution.

items.q: Which term is described by “the whole output obtained from a given quantity of a variable input”?
o: Isoquant
Average product
Fixed input
Total product
items.s: Total product is the whole output obtained from a given quantity of a variable input.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Average variable cost?
o: the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced
the addition to total expense from producing one more unit of output
the variable expense per unit of output
the fixed expense divided by the number of units produced
items.s: Average variable cost: the variable expense per unit of output. The other options describe Marginal cost, Average fixed cost, Average total cost.

items.q: Three of these relate to Market structures and price determination. Which one does not?
o: Perfect competition
Monopoly
Fixed input
Monopolistic competition
items.s: Every other option belongs to Market structures and price determination. “Fixed input” belongs to Production function and diminishing returns, not Market structures and price determination.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Sunk cost.
o: the variable expense per unit of output
an expense that rises as more output is produced
money already spent that no future decision can recover
the value of the farmer's own resources used in the business, for which no cash is paid out
items.s: Sunk cost: money already spent that no future decision can recover. The other options describe Variable cost, Implicit cost, Average variable cost.

items.q: Externality is best described as
o: a situation in which nobody can be made better off without making someone else worse off
a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction
a situation in which dealings between buyers and sellers on their own allocate resources poorly
the fall in total well-being when the quantity traded differs from the best quantity
items.s: Externality: a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction. The other options describe Deadweight loss, Pareto efficiency, Market failure.

items.q: Price floor is best described as
o: a guaranteed minimum figure at which government stands ready to buy a commodity
a store of grain held by government to steady supplies and prices
a legal minimum below which a commodity may not be sold
the regular rise and fall of prices with the farming calendar
items.s: Price floor: a legal minimum below which a commodity may not be sold. The other options describe Buffer stock, Seasonal price variation, Support price.

items.q: Average total cost may be defined as
o: the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced
the value of the farmer's own resources used in the business, for which no cash is paid out
the fixed expense divided by the number of units produced
an expense that does not vary with the level of output in the short run
items.s: Average total cost: the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced. The other options describe Average fixed cost, Fixed cost, Implicit cost.

items.q: Which of the following best describes Stages of production?
o: a factor whose quantity cannot be altered within the production period
a curve showing all combinations of two inputs that yield the same output
the range from the maximum of average output to the point where extra output becomes nil
the three ranges of a total product curve distinguished by the behaviour of average and extra output
items.s: Stages of production: the three ranges of a total product curve distinguished by the behaviour of average and extra output. The other options describe Rational stage, Fixed input, Isoquant.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Allocative efficiency.
o: a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction
the fall in total well-being when the quantity traded differs from the best quantity
the use of resources in the mix of commodities that people value most
the difference between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid
items.s: Allocative efficiency: the use of resources in the mix of commodities that people value most. The other options describe Consumer surplus, Externality, Deadweight loss.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Substitution effect.
o: a line joining combinations of two commodities that give a consumer equal satisfaction
the whole satisfaction obtained from all the units of a commodity consumed
the change in the quantity bought when a commodity becomes relatively cheaper with satisfaction held constant
the addition to satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a commodity
items.s: Substitution effect: the change in the quantity bought when a commodity becomes relatively cheaper with satisfaction held constant. The other options describe Marginal utility, Indifference curve, Total utility.

items.q: Which term is described by “the addition to satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a commodity”?
o: Law of diminishing marginal utility
Total utility
Income effect
Marginal utility
items.s: Marginal utility is the addition to satisfaction obtained from consuming one more unit of a commodity.

items.q: Choose the option that correctly defines Decreasing returns to scale.
o: the reduction in average expense per unit as the size of the business grows
a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together
a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together
the response of output to a proportional change in all inputs together
items.s: Decreasing returns to scale: a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together. The other options describe Returns to scale, Constant returns to scale, Economies of scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Constant returns to scale?
o: a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together
the smallest size at which average expense per unit reaches its lowest value
a situation in which output rises by a larger percentage than all inputs taken together
the response of output to a proportional change in all inputs together
items.s: Constant returns to scale: a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together. The other options describe Increasing returns to scale, Minimum efficient scale, Returns to scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: The total product of a variable input L on a farm is TP = 25L + 36L^2 - 3L^3. Find the marginal product when L is 2 units.
items.s: Marginal product is the slope of total product, 25 + 72L - 9L^2, which at L = 2 gives 25 + 144 - 36 = 133.

items.q: At the least cost combination on a farm the marginal product of labour is 30 kg and the wage rate is N500 per worker, while the marginal product of capital is 10 kg. Find the price of capital per unit.
items.s: Least cost requires marginal product of labour / wage = marginal product of capital / price of capital, so price of capital = 10 x 500 / 30 = 166.67.

items.q: A production possibility curve shows that a farm can produce 500 kg of maize with 100 kg of cowpea, or 550 kg of maize with 500 kg of cowpea. Find the marginal rate of product transformation of maize for cowpea.
items.s: Rate of transformation = maize given up / cowpea gained = (500 - 550) / (500 - 100) = -0.12 kg of maize per kg of cowpea.

items.q: A farm sells 500 kg of produce at N500 per kg. Its fixed costs are N60000 and its variable cost is N250 per kg. Find the profit.
A farm producing 400 tonnes at a total cost of N32000 expands to 1600 tonnes at a total cost of N96000. Find the average cost per tonne at the larger size.
items.s: Average cost = total cost / output = N96000 / 1600 tonnes = N60 per tonne.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 140 - 3Q and has a constant marginal cost of N50 per unit. Find the output that maximises profit.
items.s: Marginal revenue is 140 - 6Q. Setting it equal to marginal cost: 140 - 6Q = 50, so Q = 90 / 6 = 15 units.

items.q: At the present level of fertilizer use on a farm the marginal product of the input is 20 kg and the average product is 80 kg. Find the elasticity of production.
items.s: Elasticity of production = marginal product / average product = 20 / 80 = 0.25.

items.q: At the guaranteed price of N400 per kg, consumers demand 250 tonnes of grain while farmers supply 300 tonnes. Find the surplus that government must buy.
items.s: Surplus bought = quantity supplied - quantity demanded = 300 - 250 = 50 tonnes.

items.q: At a controlled price of N300 per kg, farmers supply 400 tonnes of grain while consumers demand 550 tonnes. Find the shortage in the market.
items.s: Shortage = quantity demanded - quantity supplied = 550 - 400 = 150 tonnes.

items.q: The marginal utilities of the first, second and third units of a farm product consumed by a household are 40, 25 and 15. Find the total utility of three units.
items.s: Total utility is the sum of the marginal utilities = 40 + 25 + 15 = 80.

items.q: A consumer is in equilibrium over two commodities. The marginal utility of the last unit of maize bought is 180 and maize costs N60 per unit. If beans cost N50 per unit, what marginal utility of beans is needed for equilibrium?
items.s: Equilibrium needs marginal utility of maize divided by its price to equal marginal utility of beans divided by its price, so marginal utility of beans = 180 x 50 / 60 = 150.

items.q: A consumer's total utility from a commodity is 300 after two units and 320 after three units. Find the marginal utility of the third unit.
items.s: Marginal utility of the third unit = total utility after three units less total utility after two units = 320 - 300 = 20.

items.q: The price of palm oil rises by 12 per cent and the quantity demanded falls by 15 per cent. Calculate the price elasticity of demand.
items.s: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity divided by percentage change in price = 15 / 12 = 1.25.

items.q: A rise of 15 per cent in the incomes of consumers raises the quantity of chicken bought by 6 per cent. Find the income elasticity of demand.
items.s: Income elasticity = percentage change in quantity / percentage change in earnings = 6 / 15 = 0.4.

items.q: Demand for eggs falls from 240 to 210 crates when the price rises from N25 to N30 per crate. Using the arc formula, find the price elasticity of demand.
When the labour force rises from 4 to 9 workers the total output of a farm rises from 240 kg to 365 kg. Find the marginal product of the extra workers in kg per worker.
items.s: Marginal product = change in output / change in labour = (365 - 240) / (9 - 4) = 25 kg per worker.

items.q: A farm's total product curve for a variable input L is TP = 40L + 30L^2 - 3L^3. Find the level of L at which the average product of the input is at its maximum.
items.s: Average product = 40 + 30L - 3L^2, whose slope is 30 - 6L; setting that slope to nil gives L = 30 / 6 = 5 units.

items.q: An isoquant shows that 500 kg of maize can be produced with 36 units of capital and 6 units of labour, or with 28 units of capital and 11 units of labour. Find the marginal rate of technical substitution of labour for capital.
items.s: Marginal rate of technical substitution = capital given up / labour added = (36 - 28) / (11 - 6) = 1.6 units of capital per unit of labour.

items.q: A poultry farm's total cost of production for the season is N470000 and its total variable cost is N320000. Find the total fixed cost.
items.s: Total fixed cost = total cost less total variable cost = N470000 - N320000 = N150000.

items.q: A farm produces 200 kg of grain at a total variable cost of N12000. Find the average variable cost per kg.
items.s: Average variable cost = total variable cost / output = N12000 / 200 kg = N60 per kg.

items.q: A farm has fixed costs of N100000 and variable costs of N200000 while producing 250 kg of output. Find the average total cost per kg.
items.s: Average total cost = (fixed cost + variable cost) / output = (N100000 + N200000) / 250 kg = N1200 per kg.

items.q: A farm's total cost is N100000 when output is 25 units and N110000 when output is 50 units. Find the marginal cost of the extra units.
items.s: Marginal cost = change in total cost / change in output = (N110000 - N100000) / (50 - 25) = N400 per unit.

items.q: When a farmer increases every input by 10 per cent, total output rises by 8 per cent. Find the elasticity of scale.
items.s: Elasticity of scale = percentage change in output / percentage change in all inputs = 8 / 10 = 0.8.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: A maize farmer sells in a perfectly competitive market at N1200 per kg. Marginal cost is MC = 900 + 50Q in naira per kg. Find the output at which profit is greatest.
items.s: In perfect competition profit is greatest where price equals marginal cost: 1200 = 900 + 50Q, so Q = 300 / 50 = 6 kg.

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 120 - 2Q. Find its marginal revenue at an output of 4 units.
items.s: Total revenue = 120Q - 2Q^2, so marginal revenue = 120 - 4Q, which at Q = 4 gives 104.

items.q: In the market for sorghum the quantity demanded is Qd = 870 - 25P and the quantity supplied is Qs = 20 + 60P. Find the equilibrium price.
items.s: At equilibrium 870 - 25P = 20 + 60P, so 85P = 850 and P = 10.

items.q: The demand for garri in a town is Qd = 1000 - 60P. Find the quantity demanded at a price of N3 per kg.
items.s: Substituting P = 3 gives Qd = 1000 - 60 x 3 = 820 kg.

items.q: One more bag of fertilizer applied to a maize plot raises output by 12 kg, and maize sells at N400 per kg. Find the marginal value product of a bag.
items.s: Marginal value product = extra output x price = 12 kg x N400 = N4800.

items.q: The marginal value product of a bag of fertilizer is N4000 and a bag costs N1000. Find the value of extra output obtained per naira spent on fertilizer.
items.s: Value of extra output per naira = N4000 / N1000 = N4.

items.q: A farm's total receipts for the season are N750000 and fertilizer accounts for 40 per cent of them. Find the amount paid out to the fertilizer supplier.
items.s: Amount paid = 40 per cent of N750000 = N300000.

items.q: A consumer pays N210 per kg for rice while the farmer receives N150 per kg at the farm gate. Find the marketing margin per kg.
items.s: Marketing margin = price paid by the final buyer less price received by the producer = N210 - N150 = N60 per kg.

items.q: Government pays a subsidy of N500 per bag on 5000 bags of fertilizer distributed to farmers. Find the total subsidy paid.
items.s: Total subsidy = subsidy per bag x number of bags = N500 x 5000 = N2500000.

items.q: A buyer is willing to pay up to N2000 per kg for rice but actually pays N1500 per kg for 100 kg. Find the consumer surplus.
items.s: Consumer surplus = (willingness to pay - price paid) x quantity = (N2000 - N1500) x 100 = N50000.

items.q: A farmer would have accepted N500 per kg for maize but actually received N1100 per kg on 30 kg. Find the producer surplus.
items.s: Producer surplus = (price received - least acceptable price) x quantity = (N1100 - N500) x 30 = N18000.

items.q: A rise of 10 per cent in the price of yam raises the quantity supplied by 6 per cent. Find the elasticity of supply.
items.s: Elasticity of supply = percentage change in quantity supplied / percentage change in price = 6 / 10 = 0.6.

items.q: The total product of a variable input L on a farm is TP = 30L + 10L^2 - 1L^3. Find the marginal product when L is 1 unit.
items.s: Marginal product is the slope of total product, 30 + 20L - 3L^2, which at L = 1 gives 30 + 20 - 3 = 47.

items.q: At the least cost combination on a farm the marginal product of labour is 25 kg and the wage rate is N300 per worker, while the marginal product of capital is 15 kg. Find the price of capital per unit.
items.s: Least cost requires marginal product of labour / wage = marginal product of capital / price of capital, so price of capital = 15 x 300 / 25 = 180.

items.q: A production possibility curve shows that a farm can produce 400 kg of maize with 250 kg of cowpea, or 350 kg of maize with 400 kg of cowpea. Find the marginal rate of product transformation of maize for cowpea.
items.s: Rate of transformation = maize given up / cowpea gained = (400 - 350) / (400 - 250) = 0.33 kg of maize per kg of cowpea.

items.q: A farm sells 300 kg of produce at N600 per kg. Its fixed costs are N40000 and its variable cost is N300 per kg. Find the profit.
A farm producing 400 tonnes at a total cost of N32000 expands to 800 tonnes at a total cost of N54400. Find the average cost per tonne at the larger size.
items.s: Average cost = total cost / output = N54400 / 800 tonnes = N68 per tonne.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 130 - 3Q and has a constant marginal cost of N40 per unit. Find the output that maximises profit.
items.s: Marginal revenue is 130 - 6Q. Setting it equal to marginal cost: 130 - 6Q = 40, so Q = 90 / 6 = 15 units.

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 120 - 3Q. Find the output at which total revenue is greatest.
items.s: Total revenue = 120Q - 3Q^2, which peaks where 120 - 6Q = 0, that is at Q = 20 units.

items.q: At the present level of fertilizer use on a farm the marginal product of the input is 12 kg and the average product is 60 kg. Find the elasticity of production.
items.s: Elasticity of production = marginal product / average product = 12 / 60 = 0.2.

items.q: At the guaranteed price of N600 per kg, consumers demand 200 tonnes of grain while farmers supply 280 tonnes. Find the surplus that government must buy.
items.s: Surplus bought = quantity supplied - quantity demanded = 280 - 200 = 80 tonnes.

items.q: At a controlled price of N400 per kg, farmers supply 200 tonnes of grain while consumers demand 350 tonnes. Find the shortage in the market.
items.s: Shortage = quantity demanded - quantity supplied = 350 - 200 = 150 tonnes.

items.q: A consumer is in equilibrium over two commodities. The marginal utility of the last unit of maize bought is 300 and maize costs N30 per unit. If beans cost N50 per unit, what marginal utility of beans is needed for equilibrium?
items.s: Equilibrium needs marginal utility of maize divided by its price to equal marginal utility of beans divided by its price, so marginal utility of beans = 300 x 50 / 30 = 500.

items.q: A consumer's total utility from a commodity is 260 after two units and 275 after three units. Find the marginal utility of the third unit.
items.s: Marginal utility of the third unit = total utility after three units less total utility after two units = 275 - 260 = 15.

items.q: When the price of butter rises by 16 per cent the quantity of margarine bought rises by 20 per cent. Find the cross elasticity of demand for margarine.
items.s: Cross elasticity = percentage change in quantity of margarine / percentage change in price of butter = 20 / 16 = 1.25.

items.q: Demand for eggs falls from 80 to 50 crates when the price rises from N40 to N45 per crate. Using the arc formula, find the price elasticity of demand.
A farm employing 10 workers produces 750 kg of grain in a season. Find the average product of labour in kg per worker.
items.s: Average product = total output / number of workers = 750 / 10 = 75 kg per worker.

items.q: When the labour force rises from 5 to 10 workers the total output of a farm rises from 120 kg to 370 kg. Find the marginal product of the extra workers in kg per worker.
items.s: Marginal product = change in output / change in labour = (370 - 120) / (10 - 5) = 50 kg per worker.

items.q: A farm's total product curve for a variable input L is TP = 20L + 48L^2 - 4L^3. Find the level of L at which the average product of the input is at its maximum.
items.s: Average product = 20 + 48L - 4L^2, whose slope is 48 - 8L; setting that slope to nil gives L = 48 / 8 = 6 units.

items.q: An isoquant shows that 500 kg of maize can be produced with 36 units of capital and 8 units of labour, or with 28 units of capital and 12 units of labour. Find the marginal rate of technical substitution of labour for capital.
items.s: Marginal rate of technical substitution = capital given up / labour added = (36 - 28) / (12 - 8) = 2 units of capital per unit of labour.

items.q: A farm produces 400 kg of grain at a total variable cost of N20000. Find the average variable cost per kg.
items.s: Average variable cost = total variable cost / output = N20000 / 400 kg = N50 per kg.

items.q: A farm producing 125 kg of output carries fixed costs of N31250. Find the average fixed cost per kg.
items.s: Average fixed cost = fixed cost / output = N31250 / 125 kg = N250 per kg.

items.q: A farm has fixed costs of N80000 and variable costs of N250000 while producing 400 kg of output. Find the average total cost per kg.
items.s: Average total cost = (fixed cost + variable cost) / output = (N80000 + N250000) / 400 kg = N825 per kg.

items.q: A farm's total cost is N250000 when output is 20 units and N252000 when output is 25 units. Find the marginal cost of the extra units.
items.s: Marginal cost = change in total cost / change in output = (N252000 - N250000) / (25 - 20) = N400 per unit.

items.q: When a farmer increases every input by 25 per cent, total output rises by 75 per cent. Find the elasticity of scale.
items.s: Elasticity of scale = percentage change in output / percentage change in all inputs = 75 / 25 = 3.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: A maize farmer sells in a perfectly competitive market at N600 per kg. Marginal cost is MC = 200 + 40Q in naira per kg. Find the output at which profit is greatest.
items.s: In perfect competition profit is greatest where price equals marginal cost: 600 = 200 + 40Q, so Q = 400 / 40 = 10 kg.

items.q: A firm faces the demand curve P = 120 - 2Q. Find its marginal revenue at an output of 8 units.
items.s: Total revenue = 120Q - 2Q^2, so marginal revenue = 120 - 4Q, which at Q = 8 gives 88.

items.q: “a market dominated by a few large sellers whose decisions affect one another” is the definition of
o: Oligopoly
Price discrimination
Barriers to entry
Duopoly
items.s: Oligopoly is a market dominated by a few large sellers whose decisions affect one another.

items.q: The correct meaning of Implicit cost is
o: the sum of all expenses incurred in producing a given level of output
the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced
money already spent that no future decision can recover
the value of the farmer's own resources used in the business, for which no cash is paid out
items.s: Implicit cost: the value of the farmer's own resources used in the business, for which no cash is paid out. The other options describe Total cost, Average total cost, Sunk cost.

items.q: In this course, Elastic demand refers to
o: the ratio of the percentage change in quantity bought to the percentage change in the buyer's earnings
the responsiveness of the quantity of one commodity bought to a change in the amount charged for another
a case in which the quantity bought changes by a smaller percentage than the amount charged
a case in which the quantity bought changes by a larger percentage than the amount charged
items.s: Elastic demand: a case in which the quantity bought changes by a larger percentage than the amount charged. The other options describe Income elasticity of demand, Inelastic demand, Cross elasticity of demand.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input”
o: Marginal revenue
Marginal factor cost
Economic rent
Elasticity of production
items.s: Marginal factor cost is the addition to total expense from hiring one more unit of an input.

items.q: Three of these relate to Agricultural prices and price policy. Which one does not?
o: Price ceiling
Price floor
Support price
Total utility
items.s: Every other option belongs to Agricultural prices and price policy. “Total utility” belongs to Consumer behaviour and utility, not Agricultural prices and price policy.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Perfect competition.
o: conditions that make it difficult for new firms to join an industry
a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities
a market of many small sellers of an identical commodity, none able to influence the ruling figure
the practice of charging different buyers different amounts for the same commodity
items.s: Perfect competition: a market of many small sellers of an identical commodity, none able to influence the ruling figure. The other options describe Barriers to entry, Price discrimination, Monopolistic competition.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Sunk cost.
o: the whole expense of production divided by the number of units produced
the addition to total expense from producing one more unit of output
money already spent that no future decision can recover
an expense that rises as more output is produced
items.s: Sunk cost: money already spent that no future decision can recover. The other options describe Marginal cost, Variable cost, Average total cost.

items.q: In this course, Diseconomies of scale refers to
o: the response of output to a proportional change in all inputs together
the reduction in average expense per unit as the size of the business grows
the rise in average expense per unit once the business grows beyond its best size
a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together
items.s: Diseconomies of scale: the rise in average expense per unit once the business grows beyond its best size. The other options describe Returns to scale, Constant returns to scale, Economies of scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the case in which quantity bought and amount charged change by the same percentage”
o: Inelastic demand
Unitary elasticity
Arc elasticity
Price elasticity of demand
items.s: Unitary elasticity is the case in which quantity bought and amount charged change by the same percentage.

items.q: In this course, Seasonal price variation refers to
o: a guaranteed minimum figure at which government stands ready to buy a commodity
the regular rise and fall of prices with the farming calendar
a payment by government that lowers the expense of an input or commodity to the user
the difference between what the producer receives and what the final buyer pays
items.s: Seasonal price variation: the regular rise and fall of prices with the farming calendar. The other options describe Subsidy, Marketing margin, Support price.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Monopoly?
o: a market with exactly two sellers
a seller so small that the ruling market figure must be accepted
a market with a single seller of a commodity that has no close substitute
the practice of charging different buyers different amounts for the same commodity
items.s: Monopoly: a market with a single seller of a commodity that has no close substitute. The other options describe Price discrimination, Duopoly, Price taker.

items.q: “a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources” is the definition of
o: Marginal rate of product transformation
Expansion path
Production possibility curve
Isocost line
items.s: Production possibility curve is a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Derived demand?
o: the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input
the addition to total receipts from selling one more unit of output
the payment for the use of land and other gifts of nature
the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make
items.s: Derived demand: the call for an input that exists only because of the call for the commodity it helps to make. The other options describe Factor share, Marginal revenue, Economic rent.

items.q: Three of these relate to Welfare economics and surplus. Which one does not?
o: Consumer surplus
Producer surplus
Average fixed cost
Pareto efficiency
items.s: Every other option belongs to Welfare economics and surplus. “Average fixed cost” belongs to Cost concepts and cost curves, not Welfare economics and surplus.

items.q: “the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input” is the definition of
o: Marginal value product
Elasticity of production
Factor share
Marginal factor cost
items.s: Factor share is the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input.

items.q: In this course, Marginal revenue refers to
o: the quantity of an input at which the money value of its extra output equals the cost of hiring it
the addition to total receipts from selling one more unit of output
the payment for the use of land and other gifts of nature
the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input
items.s: Marginal revenue: the addition to total receipts from selling one more unit of output. The other options describe Factor share, Economic rent, Optimum input level.

items.q: In this course, Production possibility curve refers to
o: the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant
the input mix at which the extra output per naira is equal for every input employed
the rate at which the output of one enterprise must fall for another to rise by one unit
a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources
items.s: Production possibility curve: a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources. The other options describe Least cost combination, Marginal rate of product transformation, Marginal rate of technical substitution.

items.q: The correct meaning of Marginal value product is
o: the quantity of an input at which the money value of its extra output equals the cost of hiring it
the ratio of extra output to average output at a given level of input use
the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input
the part of total receipts paid out to the owners of one input
items.s: Marginal value product: the money value of the extra output obtained from one more unit of an input. The other options describe Optimum input level, Elasticity of production, Factor share.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Duopoly.
o: the real or imagined differences that make buyers prefer one brand to another
conditions that make it difficult for new firms to join an industry
a market of many sellers of similar but differentiated commodities
a market with exactly two sellers
items.s: Duopoly: a market with exactly two sellers. The other options describe Barriers to entry, Monopolistic competition, Product differentiation.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Complementary enterprises?
o: the quantity of one input given up when one more unit of another is added while output stays constant
the input mix at which the extra output per naira is equal for every input employed
a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources
farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other
items.s: Complementary enterprises: farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other. The other options describe Least cost combination, Marginal rate of technical substitution, Production possibility curve.

items.q: Increasing returns to scale may be defined as
o: a situation in which output rises by a larger percentage than all inputs taken together
a situation in which output rises by the same percentage as all inputs together
the reduction in average expense per unit as the size of the business grows
the smallest size at which average expense per unit reaches its lowest value
items.s: Increasing returns to scale: a situation in which output rises by a larger percentage than all inputs taken together. The other options describe Economies of scale, Constant returns to scale, Minimum efficient scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: In this course, Subsidy refers to
o: the difference between what the producer receives and what the final buyer pays
a store of grain held by government to steady supplies and prices
a payment by government that lowers the expense of an input or commodity to the user
a legal minimum below which a commodity may not be sold
items.s: Subsidy: a payment by government that lowers the expense of an input or commodity to the user. The other options describe Marketing margin, Buffer stock, Price floor.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Supplementary enterprises?
o: farm activities that add income without reducing the output of the existing one
a curve showing the combinations of two enterprises a farm can produce with given resources
the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs
farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other
items.s: Supplementary enterprises: farm activities that add income without reducing the output of the existing one. The other options describe Production possibility curve, Expansion path, Complementary enterprises.

items.q: “a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction” is the definition of
o: Externality
Allocative efficiency
Deadweight loss
Market failure
items.s: Externality is a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Consumer surplus?
o: a situation in which dealings between buyers and sellers on their own allocate resources poorly
the difference between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid
a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive
a cost or benefit that falls on people who take no part in a transaction
items.s: Consumer surplus: the difference between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid. The other options describe Public good, Market failure, Externality.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Expansion path.
o: the set of input combinations that cost the same total amount
farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other
the rate at which the output of one enterprise must fall for another to rise by one unit
the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs
items.s: Expansion path: the line joining the cheapest input mixes for successively larger outputs. The other options describe Isocost line, Complementary enterprises, Marginal rate of product transformation.

items.q: In this course, Decreasing returns to scale refers to
o: the smallest size at which average expense per unit reaches its lowest value
a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together
the reduction in average expense per unit as the size of the business grows
the response of output to a proportional change in all inputs together
items.s: Decreasing returns to scale: a situation in which output rises by a smaller percentage than all inputs together. The other options describe Minimum efficient scale, Returns to scale, Economies of scale.
items.t: Returns to scale and economies of scale

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other”
o: Expansion path
Complementary enterprises
Production possibility curve
Marginal rate of product transformation
items.s: Complementary enterprises is farm activities in which an increase in one raises the output of the other.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Public good?
o: the difference between the amount received and the least amount a seller would accept
a service that one person can enjoy without reducing what others receive
the difference between what a buyer is willing to pay and what is actually paid
the use of resources in the mix of commodities that people value most
